title: To Thee, O God in Heaven
description: To Thee, O God in Heaven in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 378, “Baptism of a Child”, where the book credits them to Disciples' H. B.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: To Thee, O God in heaven, This lit-tle one we bring, Giv-ing to Thee what Thou hast given, Our dear-est of-fer-ing.

lines: To Thee, O God in heaven,
Giving to Thee what Thou hast given,
Where sin its purity may soil,
Where care and grief may come.
O, then, let Thy pure love,
Come down, like water, from above,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
